paras: The attempted lynching of Amsley O'Dell took place on the night of October 27, 1888, at the railroad depot in Greenville, Ohio, when a crowd of Dayton men tried to lynch O'Dell after he shot a bystander during a fight that followed a Democratic political meeting. Officers and citizens hid him in the depot cellar while the mob wrecked the building, and he was then jailed. The bystander, James M. Powell, died of his wound on November 9, and O'Dell was held on bond for the grand jury.

According to a dispatch datelined Greenville, October 30, a delegation from Dayton was waiting at the station for a train after a Democratic meeting on Saturday night when O'Dell, described as a Republican, got into a fight with someone in the crowd. Ohio state-news columns identified him as Almsley Odell of Arcanum and the place as the D. and U. depot.

O'Dell fired three shots, one of which struck Powell, a Dayton man who was standing by, in the groin. The dispatch said the Dayton men "became frantic with rage and were determined to lynch O'Dell," who took refuge in the depot as several officers and citizens tried to protect him. While some of those inside held the doors and windows against the mob, others hid O'Dell in the cellar.

The mob wrecked the lower part of the building, smashing in the door panels and window sashes. O'Dell was described as "badly used up," though the report said he would have been "torn to pieces" had he not escaped, and he was afterward taken from the cellar and placed in jail.

Powell, who had a wife and four small children, died of his wound on November 9 and was taken to his home near Dayton for burial. By mid-November O'Dell was under $2,000 bond to answer to the next grand jury. No report of an indictment or trial, or of any arrest of members of the mob, appears in the coverage.

The Greenville dispatch ran within three days in the Lancaster Daily Intelligencer, the Clarksville Evening Chronicle and the Maysville Evening Bulletin, under heads such as "At a Political Meeting" and, in Lancaster, "Killed an Innocent Man." It centered on Powell as an innocent bystander, closing that he "had nothing to do with the fight" and that "much sympathy" was expressed for him, and treated the attempt on O'Dell as a consequence of the shooting. No paper named the race of anyone involved.

Weekly papers such as the Huntsville Gazette and the Jasper Weekly Courier condensed the story into a two-sentence item in their general-news columns, placing it "at Dayton, O." and saying O'Dell was "spirited away and saved by officers and citizens." In mid-November Ohio state-news columns in The News-Herald and The Ohio Democrat reported Powell's death and O'Dell's bond, referring only to "the riot" at the depot.

The condensed national brief located the shooting and lynching attempt at Dayton, but the Greenville-datelined dispatch and the Ohio state-news brief both placed them at Greenville, where the Dayton delegation had gone for the meeting.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Amsley O'Dell
bases: A crowd of Dayton men set out to lynch the man who had shot a bystander, attacked the depot where he was sheltered, and was kept from him by officers and citizens (A2, A5).

A mob acting without authority tried to lynch O'Dell in retaliation for his shooting of Powell, but he was hidden and jailed and no one was killed by the mob (A2, A5); this was an attempted lynching, not a completed one.

The Greenville wire report (A1, A2) and the separately written Ohio state-news brief (A7) agree on the shooting of Powell by Odell at the Greenville depot and on a 'riot' there; the lynching attempt itself is described in the wire report and in a condensed brief derived from it (A5).

accounts.label: Greenville wire report
accounts.gist: O'Dell, a Republican, fired three shots in a fight after a Democratic meeting and struck Powell; the Dayton men tried to lynch him, attacked the depot, and he was hidden in the cellar and later jailed.

accounts.label: Condensed national brief
accounts.gist: In a political fight after a mass meeting 'at Dayton, O.,' Powell was fatally shot by Odell; the crowd attempted to lynch Odell, but officers and citizens spirited him away.

accounts.label: Ohio state-news brief
accounts.gist: Powell, shot at the D. and U. depot at Greenville by Almsley Odell of Arcanum 'during the riot' of October 27, died November 9; Odell was under bond for the grand jury.

framing.detail: Papers in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Tennessee ran the Greenville dispatch, headed 'Killed an Innocent Man' (as OCR'd 'Kilted art Inuecsnt Man') or 'At a Political Meeting,' stressing that Powell 'had nothing to do with the fight.'
Weekly news columns reduced it to a two-sentence item between unrelated briefs, and Ohio state-news columns later noted only Powell's death and Odell's bond.
